about: Stages and timing for the new-arrivals-launch playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: find
stages.do: Sort the new products into breakout, buried, slow start, invisible and too early, add the ones worth acting on as findings, and ask the user which to take forward.

stages.name: visibility
stages.do: For each chosen buried product, explain why it ranks where it does on its main search or category page: ranking, a rule, or recall and data.

skip_when.reason: no buried product was chosen: there's no ranking to explain.

stages.name: test
stages.do: A/B test boosting the chosen products on that page (Pattern 1), or a variant of the rule holding them back (Pattern 2), and start it after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: a boost won't help: the cause is recall, data or a redirect, or the products are already on page one.
no buried product was checked, so there's nothing to boost.

stages.name: audience
stages.do: Define and size the people with an affinity for the new products' category, with consent and an address; reuse a segment that fits, or create one after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: the new products need their data or product page fixed first: don't promote what shoppers can't find or won't buy.

stages.name: email
stages.do: Build a 'new in' email draft featuring the chosen products for that audience, after its own yes. It never schedules or sends.

skip_when.reason: there's no audience to send to.

stages.name: qa
stages.do: QA the draft until it is GO; a NO-GO fix goes back through engagement-email-builder (a new draft, with its own yes), and is QA'd again. Then wait for the user to schedule it in the Engagement UI, and record the send as a change (source engagement-ui).

stages.name: read-out
stages.do: Read the boost test's result. Don't stop early on a good-looking day.

stages.name: close
stages.do: End the test keeping the winner (or today's ranking), check every rule, then archive it, each step after its own yes.

stages.name: measure
stages.do: Measure each change from the hand-off file in turn: the boost the close kept, at full traffic, and the email launch from its send day.

skip_when.reason: nothing changed: no boost was rolled out and no email was sent.

notes.min_test_days: Days after the test stage finishes (the test started) before the read-out stage is due. discovery-experiment-setup recommends at least 14 days in whole weeks; use the end date agreed at setup when it's later.
notes.measure_after_days: Days after the latest of the close and qa stages before the measure stage is due. change-impact-tracker needs about 14 days of data after a change for a verdict other than too early to tell. The email is measured from its send day, not from when it was scheduled, so the qa stage also records the send day plus this number on the measure stage (stage --not-before).
notes.max_chosen: How many findings can be chosen at once. new-arrivals-tracker checks the ranks of up to five products and recommends grouping new products of the same type under one boost on one page; the same products go into the email. A run boosts one group on one page: products for another page need their own run.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet: the test needs longer, or the change needs more data. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on. The read-out's no_winner (inconclusive after the agreed end date) and the measure stage's other verdicts are the way out, so a run never waits for ever.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, which product it needs in a run on both (product), what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done, or after the latest of several) and skip_when (suggest skipping when an earlier stage had one of these outcomes, or was skipped; all lists conditions that must every one hold, and a condition with both outcomes and skipped: true holds for either). The marketing stages (audience, email, qa) come before the read-out so the email goes out while the boost test runs, not weeks later. A run without Discovery is offered the find, visibility, test, read-out and close stages as skips (the user names the new products); a run without Engagement is offered the audience, email and qa stages.
